newsitem.title: USA: CalEnergy sues NYSEG over list.
newsitem.headline: CalEnergy sues NYSEG over list.

text.p: CalEnergy Co Inc said Thursday it filed a lawsuit against hostile target New York State Electric & Gas in an effort to obtain the utility's list of shareholders.
In a news release, CalEnergy also attacked NYSEG's plan to offer severance packages, known as "golden parachutes", to its executives.

On Wednesday, NYSEG rejected CalEnergy's unsolicited offer to buy 9.9 percent of the utility for $24.50 per share, or $159 million. It also rejected the company's offer to start negotiations for an acquisition of all shares for $27.50 per share, or $1.9 billion.
CalEnergy, which has launched a tender offer for the 9.9 percent stake, has said it would be willing to pursue the acquisition in a proxy fight or consent solicitation.
In rejecting the offer, NYSEG said the offer did not reflect the company's inherent value, as well as other factors.
CalEnergy said it requested the shareholder list on July 22 and NYSEG refused on Thursday. The lawsuit was filed in New York Supreme Court in Tompkins County.
A NYSEG spokesman said the company will study the lawsuit and respond at an appropriate time.
